sources.excerpt: syndromes. Spinal cord syndromes may be complete or incomplete. In most clinical scenarios, physicians should use a best-fit model to classify the SCI syndrome. A complete cord syndrome is characterized clinically as complete loss of motor and sensory function below the level of the traumatic lesion. Incomplete cord syndromes have variable neurologic findings with partial loss of sensory and/or motor function below the level of injury; these include the anterior cord syndrome, the Brown-Suard syndrome, and the central cord syndrome.
